chief_data.selection_justification: Candidate 1 is the only surviving design after Candidate 2 was disqualified for exceeding pressure drop limits (41.5 bar) and bench length constraints (155.8 m). Candidate 1 achieves the required 3.0x residence-time reduction (23.4 min vs ~70 min batch equivalent) with acceptable safety margins (BPR 1.5 bar) and high conversion (0.70), fulfilling the intensification mandate for selectivity control. Warning: no concrete flow advantage identified. This design may not justify flow over batch.
chief_data.selection_rationale: Candidate 1 is selected as the sole viable flow chemistry design. Candidate 2 was disqualified due to critical hard-gate failures: excessive pressure drop (41.5 bar vs 20 bar pump limit) and impractical reactor length (155.8 m vs 25 m bench limit). Candidate 1 provides a robust solution with a residence time of 23.4 minutes, achieving the mandated 3.0x reduction over batch while maintaining a safe BPR of 1.5 bar. The primary driver for Candidate 1's success is its balanced geometry (0.75 mm ID) which keeps Reynolds number low (13) and pressure drop manageable, unlike Candidate 2's high-flow/high-pressure approach. The user objective of 'balanced' performance is met by Candidate 1's high chemistry score (0.89) and acceptable productivity (473 mg/h). The main remaining uncertainty is the exact selectivity improvement at this reduced residence time compared to batch, which must be verified experimentally. The first bench experiment should verify conversion and selectivity at the design flow rate of 0.45 mL/min.
